Abstract? Classifying sleep disorders is crucial for 
improving human health, as conditions like apnea significantly 
impact well-being. Traditional methods are often error-prone, 
necessitating accurate machine learning algorithms (MLAs). 
This research compares several MLAs using the Sleep Health 
and Lifestyle Dataset. The dataset is processed by label encoding 
variables such as gender, occupation, blood pressure, and BMI 
category, followed by MinMax scaling for normalization. It is 
splitted into training, testing, and validation sets. K-fold cross-
validation is utilized for reliable performance estimation, and 
hyperparameter tuning is conducted to enhance model 
accuracy. The parameters tuned include the number of 
estimators, learning rate, and maximum depth for algorithms 
like Random Forest, AdaBoost, and Gradient Boosting.

part of two classes are usually encoded as 0?s or ?1?s (negatives) and 1?s (positives). During a binary

elements wrongly labeled as negatives are called false negatives (FN), and the negative elements
wrongly labeled as positives are called false positives (FP).

Early diagnosis of breast cancer is exceptionally important in signifying the treatment results, of 
women?s health. The present study outlines a novel approach for analyzing breast cancer data by using 
the CatBoost classification model with a multi-layer perceptron neural network (CatBoost+MLP). 
Explainable artificial intelligence techniques are used to cohere with the proposed CatBoost with the 
MLP model. The proposed model aims to enhance the interpretability of predictions in breast cancer 
diagnosis by leveraging the benefits of CatBoost classification technique in feature identification and 
also contributing towards the interpretability of the decision model. The proposed CatBoost+MLP 
has been evaluated using the Shapley additive explanations values to analyze the feature significance 
in decision-making. Initially, the feature engineering is done using the analysis of variance technique 
to identify the significant features. The MLP model alone and the CatBoost+MLP model are 
being analyzed using divergent performance metrics, and the results obtained are compared with 
contemporary breast cancer identification techniques.
